Neat, any advice on fixing a stove?

Yes. 1st unplug it. Then, double check to make sure it is unplugged. Then find a second person to check and make certain its unplugged.
I'm used to working on systems that are 480AC and 800+DC and I will give you the benefit of my 30+ years of experience..... Don't ever work on hot systems. I have to.... UPS and power distribution equipment must almost always be energized to diagnose. 99% of my job specific knowledge is how not to kill myself. Now, that being said. If you have something unplugged, the biggest risk is cutting yourself on cheap sheet metal. Do not trust switches, fuses or anything on the machine... just because a switch is off, whatever you are working on is not safe. Unplug that shit! Another good piece of advice is PPE. Leather gloves and eye protection. I have a personal aversion to leather... wont wear it except for electrical protection.

Now: A stove is extremely simple with very few things that will go wrong.... If it is a loose wire, reconnect it using whatever method it currently uses. Screws, crimp on fitting, etc... if the fitting is damaged, buy an exact replacement. You can find the part number buy Googling the model number followed by the terms: factory service manual .pdf . somewher in the manual will be a diagram and a number that corresponds to a part number on a table on a close by page. Plug the part number into ebay and you will probably pay more for the shipping than the part itself. Make 100% certain that the wire only goes where it is supposed to and does not touch anything else... when you think you have it right, plug it in. Turn on the switch being careful to only touch the switch... don't brace your hand on the metal or lean on the stove.. You are just avoiding becoming the ground here . . If something goes wrong it will go wrong in a millisecond and trip the breaker leaving it safe again.

Just be safe... when in doubt, back out... If you have any more specific questions, let me know.
